comparisons.peer_topic: Valuation and Exclusions of Nonperforming Loans
comparisons.peer_summary: Commercial nonperforming loans were carried at 88 percent of unpaid principal balance, reduced to estimated collateral value less costs to sell, excluding loans under the fair value option, held-for-sale balances, and small business card loans.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the interaction between 'held-for-sale' status and credit quality valuation. JPMorgan reports an increase in 'nonaccrual loans held-for-sale' due to transfer activities. Bank of America explicitly excludes 'nonperforming loans held-for-sale' from its primary nonperforming loan definitions and tables, noting a specific balance of $731 million at December 31, 2024. While JPM focuses on the driver of the increase (securitization transfers), BAC focuses on the accounting treatment/exclusion of these held-for-sale nonperforming assets, showing that both entities manage and report nonperforming status separately or distinctly for held-for-sale portfolios.

comparisons.peer_topic: Consumer Loan NCLs Accounting Definitions and Footnotes
comparisons.peer_summary: Consumer loan net credit losses (NCLs) and ratios are calculated based on average loans net of unearned income, with average loans including interest and fees on credit cards. Other managed basis excludes divestiture-related impacts, and Asia Consumer includes businesses in Poland and Russia. NCLs for Asia Consumer businesses classified as held-for-sale were recorded as a reduction in revenue and are excluded from this table.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures discuss the accounting treatment of net credit losses (NCLs) for assets classified as held-for-sale. JPMorgan highlights that nonaccrual loans held-for-sale increased due to transfers for securitization. Citigroup explicitly states that NCLs related to Asia Consumer businesses 'classified as held-for-sale' were recorded as a reduction in revenue rather than in the standard NCL calculation. This illustrates a common financial driver where held-for-sale status alters the recognition or exclusion of credit losses compared to held-for-investment loans.

comparisons.peer_topic: Composition and Attribution of Equity and Debt Positions
comparisons.peer_summary: Equity positions primarily relate to investments in corporate, real estate, and infrastructure assets within Asset & Wealth Management, while debt positions include mezzanine/senior debt, corporate/real estate loans in Asset & Wealth Management, and specific held-for-sale credit card and GreenSky loans in Platform Solutions.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs disclose the existence of 'held-for-sale' loan classifications within their residential real estate or loan portfolios. JPMorgan specifically notes an increase in 'nonaccrual loans held-for-sale' driven by transfers for securitization. Goldman Sachs similarly identifies specific loan types, including 'GreenSky loans' and 'GM co-branded credit card loans', that were 'classified as held for sale' as of December 2023 (carrying forward into 2024 reporting periods), demonstrating a shared exposure to loans held for sale, although JPM's disclosure highlights a volume increase while GS highlights specific portfolio composition.

sentences.text: Loans held-for-sale and nonaccrual loans held-for-sale increased from December 31, 2023, predominantly driven by transfers of certain retained loans in anticipation of securitization and loan sales, respectively.

• Debt positions include mezzanine and senior debt, and corporate and real estate loans, substantially all of which are included within Asset & Wealth Management. Debt positions also included approximately $1.8 billion as of December 2024 and approximately $2.0 billion as of December 2023 of GM co-branded credit card loans, and approximately $3.0 billion as of December 2023 of GreenSky loans that were classified as held for sale. These held for sale loans were included within Platform Solutions.
